title: Control Evidence Stitcher and Retention Scheduler for SOC 2 / ISO 27001
text:
Control Evidence Stitcher and Retention Scheduler for SOC 2 / ISO 27001

description:
Goal: Build a platform-level 'stitcher' that consolidates telemetry and artifacts from runtime, Dedicated, and Private deployments into time-bounded compliance artifacts, and a retention scheduler that enforces region-aware retention/archival/deletion policies per SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls. The feature should let auditors retrieve a single packaged proof bundle for a control (log snippets, config snapshots, RBAC attestations, KMS audit entries) and automatically prune/ archive artifacts according to policy while preserving immutable audit trails where required.

Scope:
- Control mapping: canonical mapping of Redwood controls to SOC 2/ISO 27001 clauses (read-only source maintained by PM).
- Stitcher: lightweight orchestrator that performs incremental joins across sources (console action logs, runtime traces, bucket snapshots, KMS logs, rollout records) and produces a signed artifact manifest with pointers + hashes.
- Retention scheduler: policy engine to schedule archival (cold storage) or deletion, with region-aware exceptions and automatic evidence rehydration endpoints.
- UI surface: Console page for searching control artifacts, download bundles, and an admin view for retention policy overrides.
- APIs: read/write endpoints to list artifact bundles, trigger ad-hoc stitching for a date range, and request retention exceptions.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term archival storage provider selection, full encryption-at-rest migration, and broad changes to existing runtime telemetry formats (we will adapt via adapters).

acceptance_criteria:
A1: Given a control and a date range, the stitcher returns a bundle that includes at least: (1) config snapshot, (2) related console action logs, (3) runtime trace excerpts, (4) KMS operation logs, and (5) a manifest.json with checksums and provenance metadata.
A2: Retention scheduler can be configured per-region with rules: retain-days, archive-after-days, immutable-window-days; rules applied automatically to artifacts created after rollout date.
A3: Admin console shows retention policy applied per-bundle and provides an override workflow that records approver, reason, and expiry date for the override.
A4: Downloaded bundles are reproducible (hash of manifest stable) and a sample SOC 2 control request can be fulfilled in < 24h with the tool vs. manual process that currently takes days.
A5: Security review sign-off recorded and automated tests covering data deletion/archival paths in CI are present.

risks_and_tradeoffs:
R1: Aggressive deduplication across artifacts reduces storage but makes individual artifact provenance harder — we will keep deduplication metadata in manifest to mitigate.
R2: Synchronous stitching for large date ranges increases runtime CPU/bandwidth costs; plan to default to asynchronous jobs with a max streaming option for small ranges.
R3: Retention overrides introduce compliance risk if misused — require two-step approval and retention audit log retention for at least one immutable window.
R4: Regional deletion laws may conflict with auditing needs; retention scheduler must support per-customer exceptions and legal-hold flags.

implementation_notes:
Backend: New service 'evidence-stitcher' (stateless job runner) that pulls adapters for each source; stores bundles in compliance-buckets with server-side encryption and manifest metadata.
Adapters: small ETL adapters for console activity, runtime trace KV snapshots, rollout history, KMS audit exports. Each adapter returns normalized events with time, actor, type, and pointer fields.
Auth: use existing RBAC + dedicated service role; downloads require a signed URL with short TTL and auditor-specific access tokens.
Observability: expose per-bundle build metrics to Console (build time, bytes scanned, adapter failures) and create alert on >10% adapter failure rate.
Data protection: manifest must include hashing (SHA-256) and signer metadata; we will reuse internal signing key rotation patterns.
Backward compatibility: provide a compatibility layer to accept older telemetry formats via an adapter conversion step.

test_plan:
T1: Unit tests for each adapter and integration tests that stitch a synthetic dataset into a bundle and verify manifest checksums.
T2: E2E scenario: satisfy an example SOC 2 control request (access controls + change logs) and measure time-to-bundle.
T3: Deletion test: create artifacts, apply retention-delete rule, assert objects removed from primary storage and presence in archive metadata (if archived).
T4: Security test: attempt to download bundle with expired token and assert access denied.

notes:
2026-02-11: Kickoff with ENG (Marco, Priya), Security (Dmitri), and Compliance (Ana). Agreed to keep initial adapter surface small: console actions, runtime render traces, and KMS exports.
2026-02-25: Design review — UX mockups linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPL/Control+Evidence+Stitcher+UX. Feedback: add bulk-archive action and visibility into per-adapter success rates.
2026-02-28: ENG spike completed — prototype can stitch 30 days of telemetry for a single control in ~12min; CPU cost estimate 0.6 vCPU-hours per 30d bundle. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance/pull/412
2026-03-05: Security review notes: require signed manifests and retention override audit logs. ACTION: ENG to add signer metadata and immutable action record for overrides (ENG-4388).
2026-03-09: PM alignment: include a small export template for ISO 27001 Annex A mapping to controls; doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbCdEFgHijkl
2026-03-10: Current blockers: finalizing KMS export schema (waiting on ENG-4210) and retention policy UI slot in Console (design handoff scheduled Cycle 2026-W11).

NS2: Build asynchronous job API for stitching and add queue metrics (ENG-4388).
NS3: UX: implement admin retention override flow and add approver capture (Design: Arjun, DES-322).
NS4: Compliance to validate canonical SOC 2 + ISO mapping and provide priority control list (assigned to Ana).
NS5: Prepare a dry-run with a customer advisory group to validate retrieval and privacy constraints (target date 2026-03-31).
